args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% with healthy=false.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production, across all production regions. The initial rollback attempt halted partway with an orchestrator error after us-east completed, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1 (mixed version state). A retry completed the rollout successfully.

Current state: us-east, us-west, and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. Service reports healthy=true with error rate restored to ~0.2% (0.002).

Notes: v2.3.1-rc in the deployment history is staging-only and unhealthy; it was not used. No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Follow-up recommended: root-cause the v2.3.1 defects before any redeploy, and investigate the orchestrator error that interrupted the first rollback attempt.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Despite the timeout error, the incident was created successfully (INC-0001). Everything is complete.

## Summary

**Situation:** checkout-api was unhealthy on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (18% error rate, failing health checks).

**Target version selection:** I rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release that was healthy in production. I excluded `v2.3.1-rc` since it was a staging-only, unhealthy build. No change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

**Rollback:**
- First attempt failed partially — an orchestrator error halted the rollout after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1 (mixed-version state).
- Retried and the rollout completed across all regions.

**Verified final state:** us-east, us-west, and eu-west all on v2.3.0 — `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api documenting the failure, the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and current healthy state. The tool call returned a timeout, but I verified via `list_incidents` that the incident was in fact created and is open.

**Recommended follow-ups** (noted in the incident):
1. Root-cause the v2.3.1 defects before any redeploy.
2. Investigate the orchestrator error that interrupted the first rollback — a rollback path that silently leaves regions split across versions is itself a reliability risk.
